---
title: "What does the optimized design look like with the fuselage?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 200.0   # s for this render (rule 28)
SOLVE_BUDGET = 60.0     # s for any one solve
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import aerosandbox.numpy as np

res = optimize_glider_with_fuse(verbose=False)
sol = res["sol"]
c_root_opt = sol.value(res["c_root"])
taper_opt = sol.value(res["taper"])
cg_x_opt = sol.value(res["cg_x"])

airplane_opt = make_glider_with_fuse(c_root_opt, taper_opt, cg_x_opt)
```

**Answer.** Adding the fuselage and its mass drives the wing root chord to its maximum bound of [`{python} f"{c_root_opt:.2f}"`]{.key} m, resulting in a noticeably larger wing area compared to the bare-wing design (@fig-three-view-fuselage).

```{python}
#| label: fig-three-view-fuselage
#| fig-cap: "Three-view drawing of the optimized foam glider with fuselage."
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7, 6))
axs = np.array([
    [fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 1, projection='3d'), fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2, projection='3d')],
    [fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 3, projection='3d'), fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 4, projection='3d')]
])
airplane_opt.draw_three_view(axs=axs, show=False)
```
